definitions.explanation: An opinion or idea formed beforehand without adequate evidence or experience.

examples.japanese: {先入観|せんにゅうかん}を{捨|す}てて{話|はな}を{聞|き}こう。
{先入観|せんにゅうかん}にとらわれないようにする。
examples.english: To try not to be bound by preconceptions.

examples.japanese: {先入観|せんにゅうかん}があると{正|ただ}しい{判断|はんだん}ができない。
examples.english: You can't make correct judgments if you have preconceptions.

notes:
WORD FORMATION:
{先入|せんにゅう} (entering first) + {観|かん} (view) → view that enters first = preconception

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{先入観|せんにゅうかん}を{持|も}つ - to have preconceptions
・{先入観|せんにゅうかん}を{捨|す}てる - to discard preconceptions
・{先入観|せんにゅうかん}にとらわれる - to be bound by preconceptions
・{先入観|せんにゅうかん}なしに - without preconceptions

RELATED WORDS:
・{偏見|へんけん} - prejudice, bias (more negative)
・{固定観念|こていかんねん} - fixed idea, stereotype
・{既成概念|きせいがいねん} - established concept
